name: Edward W. Stack
current_role: Executive Chairman, DICK'S Sporting Goods, Inc. (since Feb 2021; CEO 1984-2021)
profile: Son of Dick Stack, who founded DICK'S as a Binghamton bait-and-tackle shop in 1948. Ed and his siblings bought the two-store business in the early 1980s; as CEO from 1984 he moved HQ to Pittsburgh (1994), took it public (2002) and built it into the largest US sporting-goods retailer. As executive chairman he now oversees merchandising and the Foot Locker integration.
interesting_fact: After the 2018 Parkland shooting he stopped DICK'S selling assault-style rifles and guns to under-21s, destroying about $5m of rifles in inventory, and later lobbied for stronger gun laws.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2026 Little League enshrined him in its Hall of Excellence; he played Little League in Binghamton, where his father helped grow the local program from four teams to 16.
notes: Planned to become a lawyer before joining the family business; wrote a 2019 memoir 'It's How We Play the Game'. Best route is DICK'S media relations.

name: Manfred Gorvy
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hanover Acceptances Limited (London)
profile: South African-born (1938) chartered accountant based in London who founded the private investment group Hanover Acceptances in 1974. The group focuses on real estate (Dorrington, African Realty Trust), agribusiness (Letaba citrus in South Africa) and venture capital (Fresh Capital); it formerly backed drinks bottler Refresco Gerber.
interesting_fact: In 2014 Gorvy rejected a Blackstone approach for Refresco Gerber, then one of Europe's largest juice and soft-drink bottlers.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife Lydia funded the 2011 refurbishment of a Victoria and Albert Museum lecture theatre, now the Lydia and Manfred Gorvy Lecture Theatre; they also support the National Theatre, Tate, RSC and Donmar Warehouse.
notes: Aged 88 and private; day-to-day CEO of Hanover Acceptances is now Sean Gorvy. Only route is the group's general reception address.

name: Roy Chi Ping Chung
current_role: Co-founder and Non-executive Director, Techtronic Industries (TTI)
profile: Macau-born industrialist who co-founded Techtronic Industries with Horst Julius Pudwill in 1985; TTI makes Milwaukee, Ryobi and Hoover-brand cordless tools and floor care and is a Hang Seng Index constituent. He retired as group vice chairman in 2011 and now focuses on education and youth philanthropy via his Bright Future Charitable Foundation.
interesting_fact: Nicknamed Hong Kong's 'King of Power Tools', he became a billionaire in 2021 when TTI shares surged on pandemic DIY demand.
deep_cut_fact: He moved alone from Macau to Hong Kong at 16 and started as a warehouse keeper, rising to manager within 10 years; he has since taken university students hiking and even joined them on an overseas Trailwalker event.
notes: Holds GBS, BBS, JP honours; honorary doctorates/fellowships from several HK and UK universities. TTI IR also lists ir@ttihq.com. No personal channel found; foundation or university-donor networks may be warmer routes.

name: Sam Tarascio
current_role: Non-executive Founding Director, Salta Properties (from 1 Jan 2026)
profile: Sicilian-born (1944) Melbourne property developer who emigrated to Australia aged five. A former pharmaceutical salesman at Hoechst, he built a warehouse for the company in 1972 and founded Salta Properties, now one of Australia's largest private industrial/logistics property groups (also Westgate Logistics, since sold). His son Sam runs Salta; he owns Taralinga Estate olive grove.
interesting_fact: His Taralinga Estate olive oil on the Mornington Peninsula has won gold medals at the New York International Olive Oil Competition.
deep_cut_fact: Taralinga continues a family olive-pressing tradition started around 1930 by his grandfather Salvatore 'Turi' Tarascio in Vizzini, Sicily, his birthplace.
notes: Inducted into Property Council of Australia Hall of Fame. Low media profile; route via Salta Properties general inbox. Note his son (also Sam) is Salta MD - don't confuse the two.

name: Gary Burrell
profile: Co-founder of Garmin (with Min Kao, 1989) and avionics pioneer; died 12 June 2019 aged 81 at his home in Kansas.
notes: Deceased (June 12, 2019) per Garmin announcement: https://www.garmin.com.sg/news/press-release/garmin-announces-passing-co-founder-and-chairman-emeritus-gary-burrell/ . Name in source data misspelled 'Burrel'.

name: Marco Squinzi
current_role: Co-CEO (with sister Veronica) and R&D Director, MAPEI S.p.A., Milan
profile: Third-generation owner of MAPEI, the Milan maker of construction adhesives, sealants and chemical products founded by his grandfather Rodolfo in 1937. With the company since the early 1990s, he became joint CEO with Veronica in July 2019, months before their father Giorgio died; the family also owns Serie A/B club Sassuolo.
interesting_fact: MAPEI products have been used to restore Rome's Colosseum and in the Panama City metro.
deep_cut_fact: As MAPEI's R&D chief he called research 'the brains behind Mapei's growth' in a 2018 interview, noting the group expanded from 18 to 31 research labs in three years, coordinated from central Milan labs with 170 staff.
notes: MAPEI press office (Ufficio stampa), Viale Edoardo Jenner 4, Milan, tel +39 02 37673 720, per the media-area page (email obfuscated there). His R&D/sustainability focus could fit an energy/infrastructure podcast angle.

name: Cao Ji
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Zhejiang Hangke Technology (688006.SS); also chairman of Hangke Instruments
profile: Hangzhou engineer who has spent 40+ years building reliability-testing equipment. Hangke began in 1984 testing electronic components, moved into lithium-battery back-end (formation/grading) equipment around 1998 and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019. In 2026 it took control of semiconductor-testing affiliate Hangke Instruments.
interesting_fact: Hangke was among the first batch of companies to list on the STAR Market (22 July 2019); in 2025 overseas revenue topped 50% for the first time, and it already earns revenue from solid-state-battery back-end equipment.
deep_cut_fact: The name 'Hangke' comes from its predecessor, the Hangzhou Reliability Instrument Factory ('Hang' for Hangzhou, 'Ke' for reliable), where Cao was factory director from 1984; he says semiconductors are 'our old trade' and is betting on AI data-center chip-testing demand.
notes: Strong fit for energy/data-center angle (batteries + AI chip reliability testing). Gave a July 2026 interview to STAR Market Daily (cls.cn). He was acting board secretary from May 2026; IR contacts are in SSE filings (cninfo.com.cn), not verified here. Speaks via Chinese media.

name: Pedro Grendene Bartelle
current_role: Vice Chairman, Grendene S.A.; Chairman, Vulcabras
profile: Born 1950 in Farroupilha, Rio Grande do Sul, he and twin Alexandre founded Plástico Grendene in 1971 with a loan from their grandfather, making plastic covers for wine demijohns before moving into footwear in 1978. Grendene (Melissa, Ipanema, Rider) became the world's largest sandal maker; he holds ~14% and chairs Vulcabras, where he owns ~50%.
interesting_fact: He also built Nelore Grendene, started in the 1980s, one of Brazil's largest breeders of Nelore beef-cattle bulls.
deep_cut_fact: Grendene's first sandal, the 1979 Melissa Aranha, came about after Pedro noticed the strap sandals worn by fishermen on the French Riviera; Melissa later collaborated with Jean-Paul Gaultier and Thierry Mugler.
notes: Low public profile. Grendene's press is handled by CDN Comunicação (agency). Vulcabras (run by his son) is a separate listed company with its own IR.

name: Wan Lipeng
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2014-2023) with wealth from 'CTI', shared with Wan Feng. CTI is likely Centre Testing International (华测检测, Shenzhen-listed 300012), whose chairman and controlling shareholder is Wan Feng, but no public source links the name 万里鹏 to the company.
notes: Could not verify identity or role; likely a family member of CTI chairman Wan Feng (not confirmed). Wan Feng, not Wan Lipeng, is the public face of CTI. Do not approach without confirmation.

name: Joao Alves de Queiroz Filho
current_role: Founder and Board Member, Hypera Pharma (elected Apr 2025); largest shareholder (~27%)
profile: Goiás businessman known as 'Júnior' (b. 1952) who co-founded seasonings/food firm Arisco with his father in 1969 and ran it for 20+ years. He founded Hypermarcas in 2001, built it through acquisitions, sold consumer units (to Coty, 2016) and refocused it as drugmaker Hypera Pharma; in 2025 he formed a new control bloc with Maiorem and Votorantim (~53%).
interesting_fact: Hypermarcas was pitched as a 'Brazilian Unilever' and grew by buying dozens of brands before becoming one of Brazil's largest pharma companies.
deep_cut_fact: Hypera's very first deal, in December 2001, was buying Prátika Industrial, owner of the Assolan steel-wool cleaning brand.
notes: Chaired Hypera until 2018. Portuguese IR page lists ri@hypera.com.br. Rarely gives interviews; route via Hypera IR/corporate.

name: David Sainsbury
current_role: Founder and settlor, Gatsby Charitable Foundation; Labour peer (Lord Sainsbury of Turville); former Chancellor of the University of Cambridge (2011-2024)
profile: Great-grandson of J. Sainsbury's founder; joined the family grocer in 1963 and chaired Sainsbury's 1992-97. Made a life peer in 1997, he served as UK Science Minister until 2006. A major philanthropist, he has given Gatsby over £1.7bn for plant science, neuroscience, education, Africa and the arts.
interesting_fact: In October 2026 Gatsby committed a further £77.5m to UCL's Sainsbury Wellcome Centre and Gatsby Unit for neuroscience and AI research, taking its cumulative support there above £292m.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Gatsby in 1967, just four years after graduating from King's College, Cambridge; Gatsby's £82m gift later paid for Cambridge's Sainsbury Laboratory (plant science), opened in 2011.
notes: Strong science/innovation-policy angle (former science minister; funds Babbage policy network/industrial strategy work). Best route is Gatsby's contact form.

name: James Martin Moran
profile: Jim Moran, Chicago-born auto dealer and founder of JM Family Enterprises (Southeast Toyota Distributors); died 24 April 2007 in Hillsboro Beach, Florida, aged 88.
notes: Deceased (April 24, 2007): https://www.upi.com/Business_News/2007/04/25/Car-dealer-philanthropist-Jim-Moran-dies/32871177532987/ . JM Family is now led by his family.

The only matching public figure found is Lu Yongxiang, founder and former chairman of Jilin Yongda Group (electric meters/circuit breakers; SZSE 002622), who sold his 23.81% stake in 2015-16; the company was renamed Rongyu Group.

name: Zhou Xuming
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and actual controller, Nanjing COSMOS Chemical Co. (科思股份, SZ300856)
profile: Chemical engineer (polymer chemistry graduate, ~53) who leads Nanjing COSMOS Chemical, founded in 2000 and listed in Shenzhen in July 2020. Dubbed the A-share market's 'No.1 sunscreen stock', it makes UV filters and other cosmetic actives and synthetic fragrances for clients such as DSM, L'Oréal and P&G. Revenue rebounded ~21% in the first nine months of 2026.
interesting_fact: COSMOS supplies over 20% of the global market for sunscreen UV-filter ingredients.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in polymer chemical engineering (高分子化工) and has chaired COSMOS through its 2020 IPO and its push from sunscreen agents into hair- and body-care ingredients.
notes: Low-profile Chinese industrialist; no English-language interviews found. IR contacts are in SZSE filings (cninfo.com.cn); company site blocks automated access, so not verified.

name: Song Rui
current_role: Vice Chairman, President and controlling shareholder, Chengdu Wintrue Holding (云图控股, SZ002539)
profile: Sichuan entrepreneur (b. 1975) who has run Chengdu Wintrue as president since 2005. Founded in 1995 and listed in Shenzhen in 2011, Wintrue is a major Chinese compound-fertilizer maker (9.4m+ tonnes/yr phosphate-compound capacity) integrating upstream into phosphate mining, phosphorus chemicals, soda ash and new-energy materials such as iron phosphate.
interesting_fact: Wintrue is pushing its 'resources + industrial chain' strategy abroad, investing in a potash project in the Republic of Congo and, in 2025, taking 49% of Sichuan's Mabian Shenglong mining to add phosphate reserves.
notes: Iron phosphate (LFP battery precursor) business gives an energy-storage angle. Reportedly holds an MBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business (aggregator source only). Company site blocks automated access; IR via SZSE filings.

name: Carl H. Lindner III
current_role: Co-CEO and Director, American Financial Group (with brother S. Craig Lindner, since 2005); Controlling Owner and Co-CEO, FC Cincinnati
profile: Cincinnati-born (1953) son of financier Carl Lindner Jr.; joined AFG in 1975 after a UC business degree and has chaired Great American Insurance since 1987. He co-runs the specialty property-casualty insurer AFG and co-founded FC Cincinnati in 2015, taking it from the USL to an MLS franchise (awarded 2018) and a privately financed stadium.
interesting_fact: When Meg Whitman bought ~20% of FC Cincinnati in 2019 (reportedly valuing it at $500m), Lindner said it positioned the club to 'achieve some grand ambitions'.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 Cincinnati's mayor named him and Jeff Berding joint 'Cincinnatians of the Year' for FC Cincinnati's record-setting first season; he and wife Martha also co-founded Cincinnati Hills Christian Academy in 1989.
notes: AFG press releases list Diane P. Weidner, VP Investor & Media Relations, 513-369-5713 (published business line) as contact. FC Cincinnati media office is another route; he gives local interviews about the club.

name: Doron Kochavi
current_role: Lawyer, real-estate developer and Executive Director, Buchman Heyman Foundation (Tel Aviv)
profile: Tel Aviv-born (1951) lawyer from the Buchman business family who became one of the main developers of the Gush HaGadol area of north Tel Aviv, with 20+ buildings. He is a co-owner of the planned ~$1.5bn 'Beyond Towers' (with Tidhar) and the 'Hi Tower' residential tower on the Tel Aviv-Givatayim border.
interesting_fact: He co-founded the Tel Aviv-Los Angeles sister-city partnership in 1997 and has chaired its steering committee.
deep_cut_fact: His family's Buchman Heyman Foundation, set up by his grandmother in 1942, funds the Israel Philharmonic, Tel Aviv Museum of Art and Habima Theatre and gives annual grants to young artists and students.
notes: Billionaire status is doubtful: only source is Wikidata ($1bn); a Wikipedia mirror says ~$130m. Not to be confused with tech billionaire Mati Kochavi. No published contact found.

name: Herald Chen
current_role: Director of AppLovin (APP) and GoDaddy (GDDY); adviser to AppLovin CEO Adam Foroughi
profile: Former private-equity investor who led KKR's technology, media and telecom investing (incl. its 2018 $400m AppLovin stake, WebMD, Kodak) before joining AppLovin as President and CFO in Nov 2019. He steered its 2021 Nasdaq IPO; stock options made him a billionaire as AppLovin's AI ad engine soared. Since 2024 he has advised Foroughi while remaining on the board.
interesting_fact: He sat on AppLovin's board as a KKR investor from 2018 before switching sides to become its CFO a year later.
deep_cut_fact: Alongside corporate boards, he served on the boards of Teach For America-Bay Area and the University of Pennsylvania's Jerome Fisher Management & Technology (M&T) Program.
notes: AI ad-tech/compute angle fits data-center theme. Low personal media profile; route via AppLovin press.
